verses.text: Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.
She died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went out to mourn and to weep for her.
Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and said to the Hittites,
"I am a foreigner and an outsider among you. Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead."
The Hittites replied to Abraham,
"Listen to us, sir. You are God's chosen one among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead."
Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites.
"If you are willing for me to bury my dead," he said to them, "listen to me, and approach Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf
to sell me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him; it is at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me in your presence for full price, so that I may have a burial site."
Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. So in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city, Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham,
"No, my lord. Listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead."
Again Abraham bowed down before the people of the land
and said to Ephron in their presence, "If you will please listen to me, I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there."
Ephron answered Abraham,
"Listen to me, my lord. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead."
Abraham agreed to Ephron's terms and weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the standard of the merchants.
So Ephron's field at Machpelah near Mamre, the cave that was in it, and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over
to Abraham's possession in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.
After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
So the field and its cave were deeded by the Hittites to Abraham as a burial site.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Abraham, Sarah and their family (Genesis 11:27 to 25:11)
context.audience: Israel, the children of Abraham, learning how God’s promise began
context.setting: Sarah dies at 127 in Kiriath-arba, that is Hebron, and Abraham mourns and weeps for her (vv.1-2). He rises and says to the Hittites, “I am a foreigner and an outsider among you. Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead” (vv.3-4). They answer, “You are God’s chosen one among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs” (v.6). Abraham asks for the cave of Machpelah at the end of Ephron’s field, at full price (vv.8-9). In front of everyone at the city gate Ephron offers to give him the field and the cave (vv.10-11), then names its worth: “The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, but what is that between you and me?” (v.15). Abraham weighs out four hundred shekels of silver “according to the standard of the merchants” (v.16), and the field, the cave and the trees are deeded to him before witnesses (vv.17-18). He buries Sarah in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre (v.19).
context.custom: Land sales were done in public at the city gate, before witnesses, and the boundaries, trees and price were spelled out (v.17). Ephron’s offer to give the land was a polite opening, as in Middle Eastern markets today; naming the price as “what is that between you and me?” set it high. There were no coins yet: silver was weighed. Four hundred shekels was about 4.5 kg of silver, a large sum (Jeremiah paid 17 shekels for a field, Jeremiah 32:9). Families buried their dead in rock-cut caves and laid later generations beside them.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 24 tells how Abraham’s servant went to Aram-naharaim and found Rebekah as a wife for Isaac.
context.timelineBible: This field is the only land Abraham ever owned in Canaan. Stephen says God “gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground” (Acts 7:5). Hebrews says Abraham and Sarah died in faith: “they acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth” (Hebrews 11:13), looking for a better country. Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob were later buried in the same cave (25:9; 49:29-32; 50:13).

translation.meaning: A sojourner: a foreigner living in a land not his own, without the rights of a native.
A resident alien, a settler. With ger: ‘a stranger and sojourner.’
A weight, about 11.5 grams. From the verb ‘to weigh.’ Coins called shekels came much later.
A possession, especially land held as property. The first piece of the promised land Abraham holds.

gospelParallels.note: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground.
Strangers and exiles, longing for a better country.
As foreigners and exiles, abstain from fleshly desires.

otBackground.note: Jeremiah buys a field before witnesses.
I am a foreigner, a stranger like all my fathers.
Bury me with my fathers in the cave of Machpelah.

overview.summary: Sarah dies at Hebron, and Abraham, a foreigner in the land, buys the field and cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite for four hundred shekels of silver, in public, and buries her there.
overview.settingLine: The gate of Hebron and the cave of Machpelah.

history.t: Called ‘sons of Heth,’ a people of Canaan.

archaeology.t: Herod built the great enclosure over the traditional cave at Hebron.
Stone shekel weights from Judah are marked with their value.

overview.discussion: Abraham called himself “a foreigner and an outsider” (v.4) in the land God had promised him. How does knowing I am a stranger here change how I hold what I have?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

historicalImage.caption: The Burial of Sarah, by John Martin (1833, Yale Center for British Art). Mourners carry Sarah into a great rock cave, the cave of Machpelah that Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite (Genesis 23:19).

currentImage.caption: The building over the Cave of the Patriarchs (Machpelah) in Hebron. Its great stone enclosure was built by Herod the Great in the 1st century BC; tradition holds that Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah lie in the cave below (Genesis 49:29-32).
